title: Unencoded XSS Payload Reflected in HTTP Location Header via NextAuth Error Endpoint
description: The NextAuth /api/auth/error endpoint reflects the ?error= query parameter directly and unencoded into the HTTP 302 Location header (e.g. location: /login?error=<script>alert(1)</script>). Although React Server Components Unicode-escape the value in the RSC payload and the rendered HTML body shows a fixed error message, the unencoded reflection in the Location header constitutes reflected parameter injection. This does not achieve client-side XSS execution due to the nonce-based CSP and React output encoding, but could assist HTTP response splitting in legacy proxy configurations.
evidence_safe: HTTP 302 with Location: /login?error=<script>alert(1)</script> observed in verbose curl; RSC data properly Unicode-escapes with \u003c/\u003e; HTML body shows fixed message not raw param

title: CSP Present and Nonce-Based — No CSP Gaps Identified on Frontend
description: Content-Security-Policy is present on all tested pages with per-request nonces for script-src. The policy includes object-src none, base-uri self, form-action self, and upgrade-insecure-requests. No unsafe-eval or unsafe-inline directives are present for scripts. The CSP effectively prevents exploitation of any reflected parameter injection as a script execution primitive.
evidence_safe: CSP header: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-<per-request>'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; report-uri /api/csp-report; upgrade-insecure-requests
